title: The sheaf differential relation cokernel represents derivations
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], small in the universe of its sheaf values, and let $\psi:R_1\to R_2$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings. For a sheaf of sets $T$, let $R_2[T]$ be the module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the sectionwise free modules $U\mapsto\bigoplus_{t\in T(U)}R_2(U)[t]$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], with semilinear restrictions induced by $[t]\mapsto[t|_V]$ and generator map $i_T:T\to|R_2[T]|$. Put
$$F=R_2[R_2],\qquad E=R_2[R_2\times R_2]\oplus R_2[R_2\times R_2]\oplus R_2[R_1].$$
Let $r:E\to F$ be the sheaf-module morphism defined by
$$[(a,b)]\mapsto[a+b]-[a]-[b],\quad [(f,g)]\mapsto[fg]-g[f]-f[g],\quad [h]\mapsto[\psi(h)]$$
on the three summands. Let $q:F\to Q$ be any cokernel of $r$ in $R_2$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and put $d=q\circ i_{R_2}:R_2\to|Q|$. A sheaf $\psi$-derivation into an $R_2$-module sheaf $N$ means a morphism of underlying sheaves of sets $D:R_2\to|N|$ satisfying $D(a+b)=D(a)+D(b)$, $D(fg)=gD(f)+fD(g)$, and $D(\psi(h))=0$ on every object. Then $d$ is a sheaf $\psi$-derivation and for every such $N$, composition with $d$ is a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{R_2}(Q,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Der}_{\psi}(R_2,N).$$
Its inverse sends $D$ to the unique $\alpha:Q\to N$ for which $\alpha q:F\to N$ takes $[b]$ to $D(b)$; this bijection is natural in $N$. If $M$ is an $R_2$-module sheaf and $d_M:R_2\to|M|$ is another sheaf $\psi$-derivation for which composition gives the same bijections for all $N$, there is a unique isomorphism $e:Q\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ satisfying $e\circ d=d_M$. It satisfies $e q([b])=d_M(b)$ for every local section $b$, and $e q:F\to M$ is again a cokernel of $r$.

source.place: Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, equation-define-module-differentials and proof of the representing property; Tag 04BN, definition-module-differentials, uniqueness of a representing pair.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-free-module-sheaf-universal-property] with $B=R_2$. The three assignments in the statement are maps of sheaves of sets to $|F|$: for example $([fg]-g[f]-f[g])|_V=[f|_Vg|_V]-g|_V[f|_V]-f|_V[g|_V]$, by semilinearity and the naturality of the generator map; the other checks are $([a+b]-[a]-[b])|_V=[a|_V+b|_V]-[a|_V]-[b|_V]$ and $[\psi(h)]|_V=[\psi(h|_V)]$. Extend each assignment uniquely to its free module sheaf, and combine these maps from the three summands to obtain $r$. The construction uses precisely the sectionwise free modules followed by module sheafification appearing in the item, over the same ring sheaf $R_2$. In Lean, extendGenerators constructs the three maps and freeModule_extend_inverse evaluates them on brackets. Write the combined map explicitly as fst followed by the additive extension plus snd followed by (fst followed by the Leibniz extension plus snd followed by the base extension). The identity fst followed by lift(id,0) plus snd followed by lift(0,id) equals id proves extensionality from the summands.

source.place: Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, equation-define-module-differentials and representing-property proof; Tag 04BN, definition-module-differentials.

proof.text: Use the defining property of the assumed cokernel $q$: $qr=0$, and each $R_2$-linear $t:F\to N$ satisfying $tr=0$ factors uniquely as $t=\alpha q$. Here and below juxtaposition means ordinary composition, with the rightmost map applied first. Evaluating $qr=0$ on the generators in its three source summands gives $d(a+b)-d(a)-d(b)=0$, $d(fg)-g d(f)-f d(g)=0$ and $d(\psi(h))=0$. The map $d=q i_{R_2}$ is already a sheaf map. Thus it is a sheaf $\psi$-derivation. Any module-sheaf map $\alpha:Q\to N$ is sectionwise additive and $R_2$-linear, so applying it to these three equations proves that $\alpha d$ is a derivation as well.

source.place: Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, equation-define-module-differentials and representing-property proof; Tag 04BN, definition-module-differentials.

proof.text: Given a sheaf $\psi$-derivation $D:R_2\to|N|$, the free-module bijection [lem-trf-free-module-sheaf-universal-property] supplies a unique $t_D:F\to N$ with $t_D([b])=D(b)$. Its composite with $r$ takes the three sorts of generators to $D(a+b)-D(a)-D(b)$, $D(fg)-gD(f)-fD(g)$ and $D(\psi(h))$, respectively, all zero. Injectivity of restriction to generators in that same cited bijection says that $t_Dr$ restricted to each free summand is the zero morphism. A map from the direct sum is determined by its three composites with the inclusions, so $t_Dr=0$. This equality is of sheaf morphisms; no assertion that sections of a sheafified free module are globally finite sums is needed.

source.place: Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, equation-define-module-differentials and representing-property proof; Tag 04BN, definition-module-differentials.

proof.text: The cokernel property recorded in step 2 now gives a unique $\alpha_D:Q\to N$ with $\alpha_Dq=t_D$. Evaluating at $[b]$ gives $\alpha_Dd(b)=D(b)$. Conversely, for $\alpha:Q\to N$, the maps $t_{\alpha d}$ and $\alpha q$ agree on generators and hence are equal by [lem-trf-free-module-sheaf-universal-property]. Uniqueness in the cokernel property then yields $\alpha_{\alpha d}=\alpha$. These are both inverse identities for the asserted bijection and give exactly its stated inverse formula. In particular, maps out of $Q$ are determined by their composites with $d$. In Lean, CokernelCofork.IsColimit.desc' supplies the factorization, Cofork.IsColimit.hom_ext proves injectivity, and Equiv.ofBijective packages the proved postcomposition bijection.

source.place: Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, equation-define-module-differentials and representing-property proof; Tag 04BN, definition-module-differentials.

proof.text: For a module-sheaf map $v:N\to N'$, applying its additive, $R_2$-linear components to the derivation identities shows that $vD$ is again a derivation. Associativity gives $(v\alpha)d=v(\alpha d)$, proving naturality of the forward bijection. Both $v\alpha_D$ and $\alpha_{vD}$ compose with $d$ to $vD$, so the injectivity just proved gives $v\alpha_D=\alpha_{vD}$. Thus the inverse bijection is natural too.

source.place: Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, equation-define-module-differentials and representing-property proof; Tag 04BN, definition-module-differentials.

proof.text: Suppose $(M,d_M)$ has the assumed representing property. The bijection for $Q$ at $N=M$ gives a unique $e:Q\to M$ with $ed=d_M$. The assumed bijection for $M$ at $N=Q$ gives a unique $f:M\to Q$ with $fd_M=d$. Then $(fe)d=d$ and $(ef)d_M=d_M$. Injectivity of the respective bijections at $Q$ and $M$ gives $fe=\mathrm{id}_Q$ and $ef=\mathrm{id}_M$. Hence $e$ is an isomorphism. Any other isomorphism satisfying the generator equation has the same underlying morphism by injectivity at $N=M$ and thus is the same isomorphism. The equation $eq([b])=d_M(b)$ follows by the definition of $d$.

source.place: Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, equation-define-module-differentials and representing-property proof; Tag 04BN, definition-module-differentials.

proof.text: Finally $(eq)r=e(qr)=0$. If $t:F\to N$ has $tr=0$, write $t=\alpha q$ uniquely by the original cokernel property, and put $\beta=\alpha f:M\to N$. Then $\beta eq=\alpha feq=\alpha q=t$. If $\beta':M\to N$ also has $\beta'eq=t$, uniqueness for $q$ gives $\beta'e=\alpha$, whence $\beta'=\alpha f=\beta$. This is the cokernel universal property for $eq:F\to M$, proving the last clause without any sectionwise surjectivity claim. The Lean proof constructs this new colimit with CokernelCofork.IsColimit.ofπ and proves its factorization and uniqueness using the original cokernel and the two inverse identities.
